tool_args.rationale: All five paid observations are positive and lie at H = 0.16–0.48, far short of the forecast horizon of 22.3. The slow-horizon probe directly tests whether sink-modulated fast gain gives way to endogenous adaptation and helps separate the slow amplitude from its time constant.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit the five-parameter sink-coupled dual-horizon law now
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: Over the short pilot window, the slow adaptation term mostly constrains the ratio of its amplitude to its time constant. A good pilot fit would not establish the forecast at H = 22.3.

considered_alternatives.option: Fit a static sink-inhibited saturation law
considered_alternatives.rejected_reason: It can account for gradient suppression but cannot test whether the positive short-window response reverses at long horizons.
Its slightly lower cost does not address the main uncertainty: the response at long horizons.
